raw_response:
I've been farming this same land for most of my life. Three mu isn't much, but it's mine and I know every corner of it. With just two of us at home now, I don't need to push for maximum yield — I need steady, reliable output with manageable labor. I'm 60, my back isn't what it was.

My land does wheat in winter and maize in summer, same rotation I've done for thirty years. The whole 3 mu goes to wheat after October, then straight into maize after the June harvest. I don't split the field — too complicated for 3 mu.

For **wheat**, I'll use an improved variety — something like Jimai 22 or whatever the seed shop in town is stocking from the provincial recommendation list this year. I trust those. I'll do rotary tillage before sowing — deep plowing is too much work and I sold the ox decades ago. I'll apply base fertilizer at sowing: compound fertilizer plus some urea. Then top-dress at jointing. I always irrigate three times — winter water to help the roots establish, jointing water, and heading water. Can't skip those with our dry springs here in Hebei. Two pesticide passes: one herbicide early on, one fungicide-insecticide combined around heading when powdery mildew and aphids come.

For **maize**, I buy hybrid seed every year — I stopped saving seed long ago, hybrids just yield better. I broadcast fertilizer at planting then top-dress at the big bell stage. Maize here doesn't need as much irrigation — usually one at tasseling if it's dry. One pesticide application for corn borer, sometimes two if it's a bad year.

I'm not chasing record yields. I want 450 on wheat and 550 on maize. That feeds us and leaves some to sell.
